title.zh: 卷二十三 列傳第十七 長沙嗣王業 永陽嗣王伯游 衡陽嗣王元簡 桂陽嗣王象
title.en: Volume 23: Ye, Prince of Changsha; Boyou, Prince of Yongyang; Yuanjian, Prince of Hengyang; Xiang, Prince of Guiyang
title.raw: 卷二十三 列傳第十七 長沙嗣王業 永陽嗣王伯游 衡陽嗣王元簡 桂陽嗣王象 Volume 23: Ye, Prince of Changsha; Boyou, Prince of Yongyang; Yuanjian, Prince of Hengyang; Xiang, Prince of Guiyang

sentences.zh: 梁書卷第二十三 列傳第十七

translations.literal: Book of Liang, Volume 23, Biographies 17
translations.idiomatic: Book of Liang, Volume 23, Biographies 17

sentences.zh: 長沙嗣王業 永陽嗣王伯游 衡陽嗣王元簡 桂陽嗣王象

translations.literal: Ye, Heir Prince of Changsha; Boyou, Heir Prince of Yongyang; Yuanjian, Heir Prince of Hengyang; Xiang, Heir Prince of Guiyang
translations.idiomatic: Ye, Heir Prince of Changsha; Boyou, Heir Prince of Yongyang; Yuanjian, Heir Prince of Hengyang; and Xiang, Heir Prince of Guiyang

sentences.zh: 長沙嗣王業字靜曠，高祖長兄懿之子也。

translations.literal: Ye, Heir Prince of Changsha, styled Jingkuang, was the son of Yi, the High Ancestor's elder brother.
translations.idiomatic: Ye, Heir Prince of Changsha, whose style was Jingkuang, was the son of Yi, elder brother of Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 懿字元達，少有令譽。

translations.literal: Yi, styled Yuanda, in youth had fine repute.
translations.idiomatic: Yi, styled Yuanda, enjoyed an excellent reputation from his youth.

sentences.zh: 解褐齊安南邵陵王行參軍，襲爵臨湘縣侯。

translations.literal: Upon leaving the cloth he became a staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling, acting as Annan, of Qi, and succeeded to the marquisate of Linxiang county.
translations.idiomatic: On entering office he served as a staff officer to the Prince of Shaoling of Qi, and inherited the title Marquis of Linxiang.

sentences.zh: 遷太子舍人、洗馬、建安王友。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Crown Prince Attendant, Groom, and Companion to the Prince of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Crown Prince Attendant, Groom, and Companion to the Prince of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 出爲晉陵太守，曾未朞月，訟理人和，稱爲善政。

translations.literal: He went out as governor of Jinling; before a full month had passed, lawsuits were settled and the people were at peace, and it was called good government.
translations.idiomatic: Posted as governor of Jinling, within less than a month he had brought lawsuits to order and harmony among the people, and his rule was acclaimed as exemplary.

sentences.zh: 入爲中書侍郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as Vice Director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 永明季，授持節、都督梁南北秦沙四州諸軍事、西戎校尉、梁、南秦二州刺史，加冠軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the last years of Yongming he was given the staff of authority, made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the four provinces Liang, North Qin, South Qin, and Sha, Western Rong Commandant, and Governor of Liang and South Qin, with the additional title General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: In the closing years of the Yongming era he received the staff of authority as Commander-in-Chief over Liang, North Qin, South Qin, and Sha, was appointed Western Rong Commandant and Governor of Liang and South Qin, and given the additional rank of General Who Establishes Might.

sentences.zh: 是歲，魏人入漢中，遂圍南鄭。

translations.literal: That year the Wei entered Hanzhong and then besieged Nanzheng.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Northern Wei invaded Hanzhong and laid siege to Nanzheng.

sentences.zh: 懿隨機拒擊，傷殺甚多，乃解圍遁去。

translations.literal: Yi met them as occasion demanded and repelled them, wounding and killing many; then they raised the siege and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Yi countered them as opportunities arose, inflicting heavy casualties, until the enemy lifted the siege and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 懿又遣氐帥楊元秀攻魏歷城、皋蘭、駱谷、坑池等六戍，剋之。

translations.literal: Yi also sent the Di chieftain Yang Yuanxiu to attack the six Wei garrisons of Licheng, Gaolan, Luogu, Kengchi, and others, and captured them.
translations.idiomatic: Yi also dispatched the Di chieftain Yang Yuanxiu against six Wei garrisons—Licheng, Gaolan, Luogu, Kengchi, and others—and took them all.

sentences.zh: 魏人震懼，邊境遂寧。

translations.literal: The Wei were shaken with fear, and the borderlands were thereafter at peace.
translations.idiomatic: The Wei were shaken with fear, and the frontier was thereafter secure.

sentences.zh: 進號征虜將軍，增封三百戶，遷督益寧二州軍事、益州刺史。

translations.literal: His title was advanced to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, his fief increased by three hundred households, and he was transferred to oversee military affairs of Yi and Ning and to be Governor of Yi.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, his fief was increased by three hundred households, and he was appointed to oversee military affairs in Yi and Ning and to serve as Governor of Yi.

sentences.zh: 入爲太子右衛率、尚書吏部郎、衛尉卿。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and Commandant of the Guard.

sentences.zh: 永元二年，裴叔業據豫州反，授持節、征虜將軍、督豫州諸軍事、豫州刺史，領歷陽南譙二郡太守，討叔業。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yongyuan, Pei Shuye held Yuzhou in rebellion; Yi was given the staff of authority, the title General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, command of all military affairs of Yuzhou, and the governorship of Yuzhou, and was made concurrent governor of Liyang and Nanqiao, to campaign against Shuye.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yongyuan, Pei Shuye rebelled while holding Yuzhou. Yi received the staff of authority as General Who Pacifies the Barbarians, Commander-in-Chief of Yuzhou, and Governor of Yuzhou, and concurrently governed Liyang and Nanqiao, to suppress Shuye.

sentences.zh: 叔業懼，降于魏。

translations.literal: Shuye was afraid and surrendered to Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Shuye, in fear, surrendered to the Wei.

sentences.zh: 旣而平西將軍崔慧景入寇京邑，奉江夏王寶玄圍臺城。

translations.literal: Thereafter the General Who Pacifies the West, Cui Huijing, invaded the capital region, supporting Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia in besieging the Terrace City.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward General Who Pacifies the West Cui Huijing invaded the capital, supporting Prince Bao Xuan of Jiangxia in a siege of the imperial city.

sentences.zh: 齊室大亂，詔徵懿。

translations.literal: The house of Qi was in great disorder, and an edict summoned Yi.
translations.idiomatic: With the Qi court in turmoil, an edict summoned Yi to the capital.

sentences.zh: 懿時方食，投箸而起，率銳卒三千人援城。

translations.literal: Yi was then at his meal; he cast down his chopsticks, rose, and led three thousand crack troops to relieve the city.
translations.idiomatic: Yi was in the middle of a meal when the summons came; he threw down his chopsticks, rose at once, and led three thousand elite troops to relieve the capital.

sentences.zh: 慧景遣其子覺來拒，懿奔擊，大破之，覺單騎走。

translations.literal: Huijing sent his son Jue to resist; Yi charged and struck, routing them utterly, and Jue fled alone on horseback.
translations.idiomatic: Huijing sent his son Jue to block him; Yi charged headlong and routed the force completely, and Jue fled alone on horseback.

sentences.zh: 乘勝而進，慧景衆潰，追斬之。

translations.literal: Pressing the victory forward, Huijing's host collapsed, and he was pursued and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Pressing his advantage, Yi drove on until Huijing's army broke; Huijing was pursued and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 授侍中、尚書右僕射，未拜。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant-in-Chief and Vice Director of the Right of the Secretariat, but did not assume the posts.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant-in-Chief and Vice Director of the Right of the Secretariat, but never took up the offices.

sentences.zh: 仍遷尚書令、都督征討水陸諸軍事，持節、將軍如故，增邑二千五百戶。

translations.literal: He was then transferred to Director of the Secretariat and Commander-in-Chief of all land and water forces for punitive campaigns; his staff of authority and general's title remained as before, and his fief was increased by two thousand five hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made Director of the Secretariat and Commander-in-Chief of all land and naval forces on campaign; his staff of authority and general's rank were unchanged, and his fief was increased by two thousand five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 時東昏肆虐，茹法珍、王咺之等執政，宿臣舊將，並見誅夷，懿旣立元勳，獨居朝右，深爲法珍等所憚，乃說東昏曰：「懿將行隆昌故事，陛下命在晷刻。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Donghun was wanton in cruelty; Ru Fazhen, Wang Xuanzhi, and others held power; veteran ministers and old generals were all put to death. Yi, having established the founding merit, stood alone at the right hand of the court and was deeply feared by Fazhen and the rest. They therefore said to Donghun, 'Yi is about to repeat the Longchang affair; Your Majesty's life hangs by a sun-dial's shadow.'
translations.idiomatic: At that time Emperor Donghun ruled with savage cruelty; Ru Fazhen, Wang Xuanzhi, and their faction held power, and veteran ministers and old generals were slaughtered one after another. Yi, who had won the founding merit, stood alone at the summit of the court and was deeply feared by Fazhen and his allies. They told Donghun, 'Yi is about to repeat what happened in the Longchang era—Your Majesty's life is measured in moments.'

sentences.zh: 」東昏信之，將加酷害，而懿所親知之，密具舟江渚，勸令西奔。

translations.literal: Donghun believed them and was about to inflict cruel harm, but those close to Yi learned of it, secretly prepared boats on the riverbank, and urged him to flee west.
translations.idiomatic: Donghun believed them and was about to have Yi killed. Those close to Yi learned of the plot, secretly prepared boats on the riverbank, and urged him to flee west.

sentences.zh: 懿曰：「古皆有死，豈有叛走尚書令耶？

translations.literal: Yi said, 'Since antiquity all men must die—how could there be a Director of the Secretariat who flees in rebellion?'
translations.idiomatic: Yi said, 'Since antiquity all men must die—has there ever been a Director of the Secretariat who fled in disgrace?'

sentences.zh: 」遂遇禍。

translations.literal: He then met with disaster.
translations.idiomatic: He met his death.

sentences.zh: 中興元年，追贈侍中、中書監、司徒。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongxing he was posthumously given Attendant-in-Chief, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and Grand Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongxing he was posthumously appointed Attendant-in-Chief, Supervisor of the Secretariat, and Grand Tutor.

sentences.zh: 宣德太后臨朝，改贈太傅。

translations.literal: When Empress Dowager Xuande held court, his posthumous gift was changed to Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Xuande assumed the regency, his posthumous rank was raised to Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 天監元年，追崇丞相，封長沙郡王，諡曰宣武。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianjian he was posthumously honored as Chancellor and enfeoffed as Prince of Changsha commandery, with the posthumous title Xuanwu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianjian he was posthumously honored as Chancellor, created Prince of Changsha, and given the posthumous title Xuanwu.

sentences.zh: 給九旒、鸞輅、輼輬車，黃屋左纛，前後部羽葆鼓吹，輓歌二部，虎賁班劍百人，葬禮一依晉安平王故事。

translations.literal: He was granted nine tassels, the imperial carriage, the funeral bier carriage, the yellow canopy and left banner, front and rear guard with feathered parasols and martial music, two sections of dirge singers, a hundred Tiger Guards with ceremonial swords, and his funeral rites followed entirely the precedent of the Prince of Anping of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the full panoply of princely funeral honors—nine tassels, the imperial carriage, the funeral bier, the yellow canopy and left banner, front and rear escorts with feathered parasols and martial music, two sections of dirge singers, and a hundred Tiger Guards with ceremonial swords—and his burial followed entirely the precedent set for the Prince of Anping of Jin.

sentences.zh: 業幼而明敏，識度過人。

translations.literal: Ye from childhood was bright and keen, his discernment surpassing others.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Ye was bright and perceptive, his judgment surpassing that of others.

sentences.zh: 仕齊爲著作郎、太子舍人。

translations.literal: Serving Qi, he was a Compiler and Crown Prince Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Qi he served as a Compiler and Crown Prince Attendant.

sentences.zh: 宣武之難，與二弟藻、象俱逃匿。

translations.literal: At the disaster of Xuanwu, he fled into hiding together with his two younger brothers Zao and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Xuanwu met his death, he went into hiding together with his younger brothers Zao and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 高祖旣至，乃赴于軍，以爲寧朔將軍。

translations.literal: When the High Ancestor had arrived, he then came to the army and was made General Who Pacifies the North.
translations.idiomatic: Once Emperor Wu had arrived, he came to join the army and was appointed General Who Pacifies the North.

sentences.zh: 中興二年，除輔國將軍、南琅邪清河二郡太守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhongxing he was appointed General Who Assists the State and governor of the two commanderies South Langye and Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Zhongxing he was appointed General Who Assists the State and governor of South Langye and Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 天監二年，襲封長沙王，徵爲冠軍將軍，量置佐史，遷秘書監。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianjian he succeeded to the princedom of Changsha, was summoned as General Who Establishes Might, was allotted staff officers as appropriate, and was transferred to Supervisor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianjian he inherited the title Prince of Changsha, was summoned as General Who Establishes Might with an appropriate staff, and was appointed Supervisor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年，改授侍中。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was reassigned as Attendant-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was reassigned as Attendant-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 六年，轉散騎常侍、太子右衛率，遷左驍騎將軍，尋爲中護軍，領石頭戍軍事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Regular Attendant and Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, promoted to General of the Left Rapid Cavalry, and soon made Central Guard General in charge of the military affairs of the Shitou garrison.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he became Regular Attendant and Right Commandant of the Crown Prince's Guard, was promoted to General of the Left Rapid Cavalry, and soon after was made Central Guard General with command of the Shitou garrison.

sentences.zh: 七年，出爲使持節、都督南兗兗徐青冀五州諸軍事、仁威將軍、南兗州刺史。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he went out with the emissary staff of authority as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the five provinces South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General of Benevolent Might, and Governor of South Yan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was posted with the emissary staff as Commander-in-Chief of South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General of Benevolent Might, and Governor of South Yan.

sentences.zh: 八年，徵爲護軍。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he was summoned as Protector of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he was recalled as Protector of the Army.

sentences.zh: 九年，除中書令，改授安後將軍、鎮琅邪彭城二郡、領南琅邪太守。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was dismissed as Director of the Secretariat and reassigned as General Who Pacifies the Rear, with charge of the two commanderies Langye and Pengcheng and concurrent governorship of South Langye.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was relieved as Director of the Secretariat and reassigned as General Who Pacifies the Rear, charged with Langye and Pengcheng and concurrently governing South Langye.

sentences.zh: 十年，徵爲安右將軍、散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he was summoned as General Who Pacifies the Right and Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he was recalled as General Who Pacifies the Right and Regular Attendant.

sentences.zh: 十四年，復爲護軍，領南琅邪彭城，鎮于琅邪。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he again became Protector of the Army, with charge of South Langye and Pengcheng, stationed at Langye.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he again became Protector of the Army with charge of South Langye and Pengcheng, and took up his post at Langye.

sentences.zh: 復徵中書令，出爲輕車將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: He was again summoned as Director of the Secretariat, then went out as General of the Light Carriage and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was again summoned as Director of the Secretariat, then posted as General of the Light Carriage and Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 業性敦篤，所在留惠。

translations.literal: Ye by nature was sincere and steadfast; wherever he served he left kindness behind.
translations.idiomatic: Ye was by nature sincere and steadfast, and wherever he served he left a legacy of kindness.

sentences.zh: 深信因果，篤誠佛法，高祖每嘉歎之。

translations.literal: He deeply believed in cause and effect and was devoutly sincere toward the Buddhist Law; the High Ancestor often praised and sighed over this.
translations.idiomatic: He was a devout believer in karmic retribution and sincerely devoted to the Buddhist teachings, which Emperor Wu often praised with admiration.

sentences.zh: 普通三年，徵爲散騎常侍、護軍將軍。

translations.literal: In the third year of Putong he was summoned as Regular Attendant and Protector General of the Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Putong he was recalled as Regular Attendant and Protector General of the Army.

sentences.zh: 四年，改爲侍中、金紫光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was changed to Attendant-in-Chief and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was reassigned as Attendant-in-Chief and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle.

sentences.zh: 七年，薨，時年四十八。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he died; he was forty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he died, at the age of forty-eight.

sentences.zh: 諡曰元。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Yuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Yuan.

sentences.zh: 有文集行於世。

translations.literal: He had a collected works in circulation in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings circulated in his lifetime.

sentences.zh: 子孝儼嗣。

translations.literal: His son Xiaoyan succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xiaoyan succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 孝儼字希莊，聰慧有文才。

translations.literal: Xiaoyan, styled Xizhuang, was clever and had literary talent.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaoyan, styled Xizhuang, was clever and gifted in letters.

sentences.zh: 射策甲科，除秘書郎、太子舍人。

translations.literal: In the archery examination he placed in the top grade and was appointed Secretary and Crown Prince Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He placed in the top grade of the civil examination and was appointed Secretary and Crown Prince Attendant.

sentences.zh: 從幸華林園，於座獻《相風烏》、《華光殿》、《景陽山》等頌，其文甚美，高祖深賞異之。

translations.literal: Accompanying the emperor on a visit to Hualin Garden, he presented at the seat his odes 'The Wind-Measuring Bird,' 'Hualin Hall,' 'Jingyang Mountain,' and others; the writing was very fine, and the High Ancestor deeply admired and marveled at it.
translations.idiomatic: On an imperial visit to Hualin Garden he presented at court his odes 'The Wind-Measuring Bird,' 'Hualin Hall,' 'Jingyang Mountain,' and others. The writing was exquisite, and Emperor Wu admired it greatly.

sentences.zh: 普通元年，薨，時年二十三。

translations.literal: In the first year of Putong he died; he was twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Putong he died, at the age of twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 諡曰章。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Zhang.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Zhang.

sentences.zh: 子慎嗣。

translations.literal: His son Shen succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shen succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 藻性謙退，不求聞達。

translations.literal: Zao by nature was modest and retiring, not seeking fame or advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Zao was by nature modest and retiring, seeking neither fame nor advancement.

sentences.zh: 善屬文辭，尤好古體，自非公讌，未嘗妄有所爲，縱有小文，成輒棄本。

translations.literal: He was skilled at composing literary works and especially loved the ancient style; except at public banquets he never rashly produced anything, and even when he had a small piece, once finished he would discard the draft.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at literary composition and especially favored the ancient style. Except at formal gatherings he never wrote casually, and even when he produced a short piece he would discard the draft once it was done.

sentences.zh: 十一年，出爲使持節、都督雍、梁、秦三州竟陵、隨二郡諸軍事、仁威將軍、寧蠻校尉、雍州刺史。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he went out with the emissary staff of authority as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the three provinces Yong, Liang, and Qin and the two commanderies Jingling and Sui, General of Benevolent Might, Pacifier of the Barbarians Commandant, and Governor of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he was posted with the emissary staff as Commander-in-Chief of Yong, Liang, and Qin and of Jingling and Sui, General of Benevolent Might, Pacifier of the Barbarians Commandant, and Governor of Yong.

sentences.zh: 十二年，徵爲使持節、都督南兗兗徐青冀五州諸軍事、兗州刺史，軍號如故。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was summoned with the emissary staff as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the five provinces South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji and as Governor of Yan; his military title remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he was recalled with the emissary staff as Commander-in-Chief of South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji and as Governor of Yan, his military rank unchanged.

sentences.zh: 頻蒞數鎮，民吏稱之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly took up several garrison posts, and the people and officials praised him.
translations.idiomatic: He served repeatedly at several frontier posts, and both the people and officials praised his rule.

sentences.zh: 推善下人，常如弗及。

translations.literal: He advanced others' goodness and lowered himself before men, always as if he could not match them.
translations.idiomatic: He deferred to others' virtues and humbled himself before all, always as though he fell short of them.

sentences.zh: 徵爲太子詹事。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 普通三年，遷領軍將軍，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the third year of Putong he was transferred to General of the Garrison Guards and given the additional title Attendant-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Putong he was promoted to General of the Garrison Guards with the additional title Attendant-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 六年，爲軍師將軍，與西豊侯正德北伐渦陽，輒班師，爲有司所奏，免官削爵土。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made General of the Army and, with the Marquis of Xifeng, Zhengde, marched north against Woyang; he abruptly withdrew the army, was impeached by the responsible offices, and was stripped of office and fief.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he served as General of the Army and joined the Marquis of Xifeng, Zhengde, on a northern campaign against Woyang, but abruptly withdrew his forces. The authorities impeached him, and he was stripped of office and fief.

sentences.zh: 七年，起爲宗正卿。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was raised up as Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was reappointed Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 八年，復封爵，尋除左衛將軍，領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: In the eighth year his title was restored; soon he was appointed General of the Left Guard and made Commandant of Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year his title was restored; soon after he was appointed General of the Left Guard and Commandant of Foot Soldiers.

sentences.zh: 大通元年，遷侍中、中護軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Datong he was transferred to Attendant-in-Chief and Central Guard General.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Datong he was promoted to Attendant-in-Chief and Central Guard General.

sentences.zh: 時渦陽始降，乃以藻爲使持節、北討都督、征北大將軍，鎮于渦陽。

translations.literal: At that time Woyang had just surrendered, and Zao was made emissary with staff of authority, Northern Campaign Commander-in-Chief, and General Who Conquers the North, stationed at Woyang.
translations.idiomatic: Woyang had just surrendered, and Zao was appointed with the emissary staff as Northern Campaign Commander-in-Chief and General Who Conquers the North, with his headquarters at Woyang.

sentences.zh: 二年，爲中權將軍、金紫光祿大夫，置佐史，加侍中。

translations.literal: In the second year he was made General of Central Authority, Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle, with staff officers allotted, and given the additional title Attendant-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed General of Central Authority and Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Girdle with an appropriate staff, and given the additional title Attendant-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 中大通元年，遷護軍將軍，中權如故。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongdatong he was transferred to Protector General of the Army; his title of Central Authority remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhongdatong he was promoted to Protector General of the Army while retaining his rank as General of Central Authority.

sentences.zh: 三年，爲中軍將軍、太子詹事，出爲丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the third year he was made Central Army General and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, then went out as Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed Central Army General and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, then posted as Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 高祖每歎曰：「子弟並如迦葉，吾復何憂。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor often sighed and said, 'If all my sons and younger kinsmen were like Kaye, what would I have to worry about?'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu often sighed and said, 'If all my sons and nephews were like Kaye, what would I have to worry about?'

sentences.zh: 」迦葉，藻小名也。

translations.literal: Kaye was Zao's childhood name.
translations.idiomatic: Kaye was Zao's childhood name.

sentences.zh: 入爲安左將軍、尚書左僕射，加侍中，藻固辭不就，詔不許。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as General Who Pacifies the Left and Vice Director of the Left of the Secretariat, with the additional title Attendant-in-Chief; Zao firmly declined and would not accept, but the edict did not permit it.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as General Who Pacifies the Left and Vice Director of the Left of the Secretariat with the additional title Attendant-in-Chief. Zao firmly declined, but the edict would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 大同五年，遷中衛將軍、開府儀同三司、中書令，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Datong he was transferred to Central Guard General, Commander with honor equal to the Three Excellencies and an office of his own, and Director of the Secretariat; his title as Attendant-in-Chief remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Datong he was promoted to Central Guard General, Commander with honors equal to the Three Excellencies and his own staff, and Director of the Secretariat, while retaining his title as Attendant-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 藻性恬靜，獨處一室，床有膝痕，宗室衣冠，莫不楷則。

translations.literal: Zao by nature was tranquil and still; he dwelt alone in a single room, and his couch bore the marks of his knees. Among the imperial clan and the gentry, none did not take him as a model.
translations.idiomatic: Zao was tranquil by nature. He lived alone in a single room, and the marks of his knees were worn into his couch. Throughout the imperial clan and the gentry, all looked to him as a model.

sentences.zh: 常以爵祿太過，每思摒退，門庭閑寂，賓客罕通，太宗尤敬愛之。

translations.literal: He often felt his rank and stipend were excessive and always thought of withdrawing; his gates and courtyard were quiet and still, and guests rarely came. The Crown Prince especially revered and loved him.
translations.idiomatic: He often felt his rank and stipend were too great and always thought of resigning. His household was quiet and still, and guests rarely called. Crown Prince Zhao especially revered and loved him.

sentences.zh: 自遭家禍，恒布衣蒲席，不食鮮禽，非在公庭，不聽音樂。

translations.literal: Since the family disaster he always wore plain cloth and sat on rush mats, ate no fresh poultry, and unless in the public court did not listen to music.
translations.idiomatic: Since his family's tragedy he always wore plain cloth and sat on rush mats, ate no fresh meat or poultry, and listened to no music except on formal court occasions.

sentences.zh: 高祖每以此稱之。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor often praised him for this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu often praised him for this.

sentences.zh: 出爲使持節、督南徐州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out with the emissary staff of authority as overseer and Governor of South Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted with the emissary staff as Governor of South Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 侯景亂，藻遣長子彧率兵入援，及城開，加散騎常侍、大將軍。

translations.literal: In the disorder of Hou Jing, Zao sent his eldest son Yu to lead troops in relief; when the city was opened he was given the additional titles Regular Attendant and Great General.
translations.idiomatic: During Hou Jing's rebellion, Zao sent his eldest son Yu to lead troops to relieve the capital. When the city fell he was given the additional titles Regular Attendant and Great General.

sentences.zh: 景遣其儀同蕭邕代之，據京口，藻因感氣疾，不自療。

translations.literal: Jing sent his Yitong Xiao Yong to replace him and seized Jingkou; Zao therefore fell ill with ch'i disorder and did not treat himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hou Jing sent his officer Xiao Yong to replace him and seized Jingkou. Zao fell ill with a wasting disorder and refused to seek treatment.

sentences.zh: 或勸奔江北，藻曰：「吾國之台鉉，位任特隆，旣不能誅剪逆賊，正當同死朝廷，安能投身異類，欲保餘生。

translations.literal: Some urged him to flee north of the river; Zao said, 'I am a pillar of the state, my position and commission exceptionally lofty. Having failed to cut down the rebel bandits, I should rightly die together with the court—how could I cast myself among alien kinds to preserve what life remains?'
translations.idiomatic: Some urged him to flee north of the Yangzi. Zao said, 'I am a pillar of the state, my rank and responsibility exceptionally great. Having failed to destroy the rebels, I ought to die with the court. How could I cast my lot among alien peoples merely to preserve what life remains?'

sentences.zh: 」因不食累日。

translations.literal: He therefore did not eat for many days.
translations.idiomatic: He then refused food for many days.

sentences.zh: 太清三年，薨，時年六十七。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taiqing he died; he was sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taiqing he died, at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 伯游美風神，善言玄理。

translations.literal: Boyou had fine bearing and spirit and was skilled at speaking of the dark principle.
translations.idiomatic: Boyou had an elegant bearing and was skilled in the discourse of metaphysics.

sentences.zh: 天監元年四月，詔曰：「兄子伯游，雖年識未弘，意尚粗可。

translations.literal: In the fourth month of the first year of Tianjian an edict said, 'My elder brother's son Boyou, though his years and knowledge are not yet broad, his intentions are still roughly acceptable.'
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of the first year of Tianjian an edict read, 'My elder brother's son Boyou, though still young in years and learning, shows promise of sound judgment.'

sentences.zh: 浙東奧區，宜須撫蒞，可督會稽東陽新安永嘉臨海五郡諸軍事、輔國將軍、會稽太守。

translations.literal: The vital region of eastern Zhe must be soothed and overseen; he may be made Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the five commanderies Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Yongjia, and Linhai, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: The vital region of eastern Zhe requires a steady hand; he is appointed Commander-in-Chief of Kuaiji, Dongyang, Xin'an, Yongjia, and Linhai, General Who Assists the State, and Governor of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 」二年，襲封永陽郡王。

translations.literal: In the second year he succeeded to the princedom of Yongyang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he inherited the title Prince of Yongyang.

sentences.zh: 五年，薨，時年二十三。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he died; he was twenty-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he died, at the age of twenty-three.

sentences.zh: 諡曰恭。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Gong.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Gong.

sentences.zh: 元簡三年襲封，除中書郎，遷會稽太守。

translations.literal: Yuanjian in the third year succeeded to the fief, was appointed Secretary of the Secretariat, and was transferred to Governor of Kuaiji.
translations.idiomatic: Yuanjian inherited the title in the third year, was appointed Secretary of the Secretariat, and was then transferred to Governor of Kuaiji.

sentences.zh: 十三年，入爲給事黃門侍郎，出爲持節、都督廣交越三州諸軍事、平越中郎將、廣州刺史。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he entered the capital as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, then went out with the staff of authority as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the three provinces Guang, Jiao, and Yue, General of the Interior Who Pacifies Yue, and Governor of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was recalled as Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate, then posted with the staff of authority as Commander-in-Chief of Guang, Jiao, and Yue, General of the Interior Who Pacifies Yue, and Governor of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 還爲太子中庶子，遷使持節、都督郢司霍三州諸軍事、信武將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: He returned and became Attendant of the Crown Prince, then was transferred with the emissary staff of authority as Commander-in-Chief of all military affairs of the three provinces E, Si, and Huo, General of Trustworthy Might, and Governor of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Attendant of the Crown Prince, then was posted with the emissary staff as Commander-in-Chief of E, Si, and Huo, General of Trustworthy Might, and Governor of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 十八年正月，卒於州。

translations.literal: In the first month of the eighteenth year he died in the province.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the eighteenth year he died in office.

sentences.zh: 諡曰孝。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Xiao.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Xiao.

sentences.zh: 子俊嗣。

translations.literal: His son Jun succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jun succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 象容止閒雅，善於交遊，事所生母以孝聞。

translations.literal: Xiang's bearing and deportment were easy and refined; he was skilled at social intercourse, and in serving the mother who bore him he was famed for filial piety.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang had an easy, refined bearing and was skilled in society. In caring for his birth mother he was renowned for filial devotion.

sentences.zh: 起家寧遠將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: Upon first taking office he was made General Who Pacifies the Distance and Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: On entering office he was appointed General Who Pacifies the Distance and Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 到官未幾，簡王妃薨，去職。

translations.literal: He had not long been in the post when the Princess of Jian died, and he left office.
translations.idiomatic: He had not long taken up his post when the Princess of Jian died, and he resigned to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 服闋，復授明威將軍、丹陽尹。

translations.literal: When mourning was completed he was again given the title General of Bright Might and Governor of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: When his mourning period ended he was reappointed General of Bright Might and Governor of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 象生長深宮，始親庶政，舉無失德，朝廷稱之。

translations.literal: Xiang had grown up in the deep palace; when he first took part in ordinary government affairs, in all he did there was no lapse in virtue, and the court praised him.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang had grown up within the palace walls. When he first took up the duties of government, nothing he did fell short of propriety, and the court praised him.

sentences.zh: 出爲持節、督司霍郢三州諸軍事、征遠將軍、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: He went out with the staff of authority as overseer of all military affairs of the three provinces Si, Huo, and E, General Who Campaigns Afar, and Governor of Ezhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted with the staff of authority as overseer of Si, Huo, and E, General Who Campaigns Afar, and Governor of Ezhou.

sentences.zh: 尋遷湘衡二州諸軍事、輕車將軍、湘州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to oversee military affairs of the two provinces Xiang and Heng, General of the Light Carriage, and Governor of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was transferred to oversee military affairs in Xiang and Heng, as General of the Light Carriage and Governor of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 湘州舊多虎暴，及象在任，爲之靜息，故老咸稱德政所感。

translations.literal: Xiangzhou in former times had many violent tigers; when Xiang was in office they were stilled and quieted, and the elders all said it was moved by his virtuous government.
translations.idiomatic: Xiangzhou had long been troubled by man-eating tigers. Under Xiang's rule they ceased their depredations, and the elders all attributed it to the power of his virtuous rule.

sentences.zh: 除中書侍郎，俄以本官行石頭戍軍事，轉給事黃門侍郎、兼領軍，又以本官兼宗正卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat; soon, in his present office, he acted in the military affairs of the Shitou garrison; he was transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrent General of the Garrison Guards, and again in his present office was made concurrent Director of the Imperial Clan.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director of the Secretariat, and soon afterward acted in his existing capacity over the military affairs of the Shitou garrison. He was then transferred to Attendant Gentleman of the Yellow Gate and concurrent General of the Garrison Guards, and concurrently served as Director of the Imperial Clan.

sentences.zh: 尋遷侍中、太子詹事，未拜，改授持節、督江州諸軍事、信武將軍、江州刺史。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to Attendant-in-Chief and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince; he did not assume the posts and was reassigned with the staff of authority as overseer of all military affairs of Jiangzhou, General of Trustworthy Might, and Governor of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was promoted to Attendant-in-Chief and Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince, but before he could take up those offices he was reassigned with the staff of authority as overseer of Jiangzhou, General of Trustworthy Might, and Governor of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 以疾免。

translations.literal: Because of illness he was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He resigned on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 尋除太常卿，加侍中，遷秘書監、領步兵校尉。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Director of the Imperial Sacrifices, given the additional title Attendant-in-Chief, and transferred to Supervisor of the Secretariat and Commandant of Foot Soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after he was appointed Director of the Imperial Sacrifices with the additional title Attendant-in-Chief, and was then made Supervisor of the Secretariat and Commandant of Foot Soldiers.

sentences.zh: 大同二年，薨，諡曰敦。

translations.literal: In the second year of Datong he died; his posthumous title was Dun.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Datong he died and was given the posthumous title Dun.

sentences.zh: 子慥嗣。

translations.literal: His son Cao succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: His son Cao succeeded him.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：長沙諸嗣王，並承襲土宇，光有籓服。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: The various Heir Princes of Changsha all inherited their domains and shone with the glory of their fiefdoms.
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: The successive Heir Princes of Changsha all inherited their domains and brought honor to their princely houses.

sentences.zh: 桂陽王象以孝聞，在於牧湘，猛虎息暴，蓋德惠所致也。

translations.literal: Prince Xiang of Guiyang was famed for filial piety; when he governed Xiang, fierce tigers ceased their violence—surely this was brought about by his virtue and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Xiang of Guiyang was renowned for filial devotion. When he governed Xiangzhou, the man-eating tigers ceased their ravages—surely the effect of his benevolent rule.

sentences.zh: 昔之善政，何以加焉。

translations.literal: How could the good government of old surpass this?
translations.idiomatic: What good government of antiquity could surpass this?

translations.literal: Note 1.
translations.idiomatic: Note 1.

sentences.zh: 全文以中華書局、一九七三年五月版《梁書》爲本校。

translations.idiomatic: The full text has been collated against the Zhonghua Shuju edition of the 《Book of Liang》, May 1973.
